headline: High-risk shared-workspace and plugin/API interaction: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAI-style tools while marker is a document processor with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can ingest files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools, while marker is a document-processing agent. If marker outputs are fed into SK through a shared workspace or plugin path, attacker-controlled document content can be treated as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is an interaction risk rather than a proven exploit.
conditions: IF marker outputs are copied into a Semantic Kernel plugin input or shared file without sanitization, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF an MCP server or file bridge is added between the agents, instruction hijacking risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of marker outputs into SK prompts.
Add a strict content/schema separator between document text and instructions.
Require manual review before any MCP tool call on marker-produced content.
Use allowlisted file paths for any shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker is docs-only and shows no filesystem read/write or network egress, but Semantic Kernel can read files, write files, and call external APIs. If both agents share a workspace, marker content can flow into SK and then out to third-party model providers or plugins. The pair therefore has a default leakage path once shared files are used.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, marker-produced documents can be read by SK.
IF SK is configured with external model providers or plugins, shared file contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate directories or volumes.
Turn off SK access to sensitive folders.
Restrict SK plugins to local-only endpoints.
Redact secrets from marker outputs before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker has no write, shell, or git capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable state. Semantic Kernel can write files, but the pair only conflicts if the operator deliberately points both at the same writable path or shared plugin state. The blast radius is limited to local file overwrites, not broad system compromise.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF SK instances share memory-store state, concurrent updates can race on shared records.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories per agent.
Avoid shared git worktrees for the pair.
Serialize writes to any shared memory store.
Use per-run filenames with timestamps or UUIDs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs, while marker produces document-processing results that SK may treat as authoritative input. If marker extraction errors are forwarded without verification, SK can propagate bad facts into downstream actions. The pair is not inherently dangerous, but the default agent-to-agent handoff can amplify mistakes.
conditions: IF SK consumes marker output as ground truth without validation, extraction errors can cascade.
IF SK is connected to action-taking plugins, a bad document parse can trigger incorrect downstream actions.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before SK uses marker output.
Require citations or page references for extracted claims.
Limit SK actions to read-only mode during initial runs.
Sample-check a few outputs against source documents.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection logic.

E_compliance.rationale: Marker's profile shows no data classes touched, while Semantic Kernel explicitly handles application context and secrets and can call external APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is processed through SK, residency and retention depend on the chosen model providers and plugins, which are not constrained by default. The compliance risk is therefore configuration-dependent but real.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through SK plugins or external model providers, residency and retention obligations may be violated.
IF the operator uses SK with secrets-handling plugins, logging policy must match the data class.
mitigations: Route only non-sensitive data through SK.
Choose providers with documented residency and retention terms.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Review plugin data handling before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
